transcript.text: I need to flag a load-in issue. During this week's load test, I measured the Orpheum's loading-dock lift and it has a hard 900-kilogram limit. Our drafted rotating scenic unit weighs 1,100 kilograms, so it won't fit as currently designed. The good news is that splitting it into two 550-kilogram modules is workable. I haven't updated the load-in drawing yet, but I can do that once we agree on the approach.

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights clearance issue. I confirmed with the archive licensor yesterday that the special's historical comedy clips are cleared for the theater recording and domestic broadcast, but they are NOT cleared for online replay. I have not yet entered this restriction in the distribution worksheet, so the current plan's online replay component would violate our clip licensing terms unless we either remove the clips from the replay or secure additional clearance.

transcript.text: I need to flag an insurance requirement. I obtained the insurer's written event endorsement this morning, and it specifies that the audience must be seated in three blocks separated by two unobstructed aisles, each at least 1.2 meters wide, for our coverage to remain valid. This conflicts with the current draft plan, which seats the audience in two blocks. I should note that the endorsement is currently attached to my email rather than the production file, so I'll make sure it gets filed properly. We'll need to revise the seating plan to three blocks with the required aisle spacing, or we risk invalidating our insurance coverage for the event.
